newsitem.title: USA: Officials say Clinton to name Tenet as CIA nominee.
newsitem.headline: Officials say Clinton to name Tenet as CIA nominee.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has decided to nominate George Tenet, the current acting head of the CIA, to serve as director of the U.S. spy agency, senior administration officials said on Wednesday.
"The president believes he (Tenet) is well qualified for the post," said one senior White House official. "He's more than satisfied."

The nomination of Tenet, 44, who was deputy CIA director before interim appointment as acting director last December, replaces that of Anthony Lake, who withrew from consideration on Monday after harsh Senate confirmation hearings.

Tenet, a close friend of Lake's, was unlikely to encounter similar stiff opposition in winning Senate confirmation. He has served as staff director of the Senate Intelligence Committee, which anchors the confirmation process, and underwent scrutiny when confirmed as deputy CIA director.
Administration officials said Clinton was likely to make the formal announcement before he departed on Wednesday night for a summit in Helsinki with Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
